correctness.rationale: With a=d²S/(4T)>0 and normalized by the constant pumping rate, the step response D(t)=erfc(√(a/t)) extends by zero at t≤0. Its derivative is q(t)=√(a/π)t^(−3/2)e^(−a/t), with q(0)=0. Linear superposition gives D(t)−D(t−τ); the derivative is positive during pumping, and afterwards is q(t)−q(t−τ). Independently, log q has derivative a/t²−3/(2t), giving the unique mode m=2a/3. If t>τ and t≤m, both arguments are on the increasing side and the difference is positive; if t≥τ+m it is negative. On max(τ,m)<t<τ+m, q(t) decreases and q(t−τ) increases, and the endpoint signs are respectively positive and negative, including t=τ via q(0)=0. There is therefore one strict global peak, with the claimed strict bounds. Equality of the kernels gives the stated logarithmic equation with the same sign and constants. Implicit differentiation gives dt*/dτ=q′(t*−τ)/[q′(t*−τ)−q′(t*)] in (0,1); the lag decreases. The bracket gives t*→m as τ↓0 and the equality on the increasing branch gives t*−τ→0 as τ→∞. This is an analytic check; no finite sample is required.
residual_risks: Only the ideal linear fixed-stage model and one rectangular pulse are covered; this is a peak in rate, not cumulative depletion or drawdown.
